notice: Guided ADE elicitation contract: what the Primary ADE must do when it conducts the Initial Design Questionnaire. The CLI performs only the handoff (template.materialize, then hands the working copy to the Primary ADE). Content, questions, structure and evolution belong to the questionnaire itself; each directive cites where the questionnaire states it.

handoff.next_action: Open the project in the Primary ADE and write anything: its first answer starts the Initial Design Questionnaire, or resumes it where it stopped. /gtt starts it explicitly where the ADE supports it.

start.statement: While the questionnaire is pending or in-progress and the project is not frozen, the Primary ADE starts or resumes the interview in its first answer of a session, whatever the user's first message says, and whenever the user asks for it explicitly (/gtt where the ADE supports it). It does not wait to be told where the questionnaire is.
start.applies_to: every ADE: the instruction is in AGENTS.md -> Bootstrap behavior; the computed state reaches the session through gtt-domain/session.md (## Next action)
start.never: an interruption of ordinary work the user asked for in that message: the ADE says in one line that the questionnaire is open and offers to resume it, then does what was asked

state.pending: the working copy is as materialized: no section answered, no provenance tag added, no THINK Depth, no readiness
state.complete: readiness READY or READY_WITH_OPEN_ITEMS (section 23) with every minimum-floor line MET, and the human review recorded (section 24); a copy without the review record or the floor table is judged on what it has
state.next_action: shown in gtt-domain/session.md only while the state is pending or in-progress and gtt-domain/.frozen does not exist
state.authority: none: derived operational state, never a decision, never evidence

persistence.where: the working copy itself (handoff.template materialized at its declared location); nothing else holds progress
rules: Write what each round established into the working copy before asking the next round.
On resume, read the working copy first and never ask again what it already answers; an answer is revisited only when new information creates a [CONFLICTO].
Never overwrite or reword an answer the human gave; a correction from the human is recorded next to it, with the date.
Never turn a [PROPUESTA] into an answer, a confirmed decision or a 'Human decision' entry; only the human's explicit confirmation in the conversation does, and it is recorded as theirs.
Record the human review (section 24) only when the human has said the summary reflects their understanding.

directives.text: Inspect the project before asking anything that existing evidence answers.
Ask progressively, never the whole form at once.
directives.questionnaire: 2. Important Rule: Do Not Interrogate the User With the Whole Form

directives.text: Do not ask what the project already establishes.
Keep unknowns visible as [VACÍO]; keep a list of relevant unknowns.
Expose disagreements between sources or answers as [CONFLICTO]; never choose a winner silently.
Mark every option you suggest as [PROPUESTA]; a proposal is never a decision.
Attribute what the project shows with [FUENTE: file:line]; preserve the human's wording for requirements.
Ask for explicit human confirmation whenever an architectural decision is required; never fill 'Human decision' for the human.
Never invent an architectural decision to complete a section.
Open every message of the interview with `@gtt · Initial Design Questionnaire`; the marker identifies the speaker and is never a decision.
Ask one question per message (two only when they are about the same thing); never a list of questions, a whole section or a menu followed by more questions.
directives.questionnaire: 2. Important Rule: Do Not Interrogate the User With the Whole Form

directives.text: The human's own messages in the conversation are evidence: record what they already answer, say back what you understood, and never ask again for what they gave.
directives.questionnaire: 2. Important Rule: Do Not Interrogate the User With the Whole Form

directives.text: Ask in plain words and in the human's language, about their project and not about GTT; technical questions only when they matter, as a short choice with 'I don't know yet' as a valid answer.
directives.questionnaire: 2. Important Rule: Do Not Interrogate the User With the Whole Form

directives.text: Reach the architecture and the stack before the interview ends: ask every line of the minimum floor at every depth, QUICK included; a readiness above NOT_READY requires every line MET by the human.

Offer numbered options for every question so the human can answer with a number: options from the evidence, the recommendation marked, "I don't know yet" and a last "Other (write it)"; writing is always allowed, never required.
directives.questionnaire: 2. Important Rule: Do Not Interrogate the User With the Whole Form

think_depth.statement: THINK Depth is how deep the Think stage goes: how much the ADE assesses, explores and asks. It is never a level of governance. It changes how far THINK digs, never which rules THINK may skip.
think_depth.not_a_method_plan: THINK Depth is independent of the Autonomy Profile and shares no name with it. It is never derived from the plan, and it never changes a plan's gates.

selection.policy: ask once near the start, as one plain question offering the three levels; never inferred from the project, the Autonomy Profile, the ADE or a previous project

unselected.note: STANDARD is the behaviour that existed before depths; it applies as a fallback and is never reported as a choice

recorded_in: the Design Assessment working copy (THINK Depth section) when a design document exists
the questionnaire working copy (THINK Depth section) when there is none

invariant_at_every_depth: the minimum floor of the Design Assessment, assessed line by line
the Minimum Viable Governed Design of the questionnaire
the evidence boundary and the provenance tags: [FUENTE], [VACIO], [CONFLICTO], [PROPUESTA]
human decision authority: the ADE takes part in THINK and decides nothing
freeze semantics and the pre-freeze / post-freeze regimes
the original documents are never modified
the assessment is a working artifact, never governed context

QUICK.assessment: Rate the floor areas always, and the other areas the documents make relevant; an area left out is written as `not assessed (QUICK)`, never as SOLID.
QUICK.focus: critical gaps: whatever keeps the floor from being met or would make the design unbuildable
QUICK.stack: Options only for a floor layer that is undecided: one recommendation with its main trade-off, as [PROPUESTA].
QUICK.questionnaire: Reduced: only the areas rated THIN or MISSING that the floor or a critical gap needs. No exploration beyond them.

STANDARD.assessment: The complete assessment: every area rated with its evidence.
STANDARD.focus: every area rated THIN or MISSING
STANDARD.stack: Reasonable alternatives for each undecided or unjustified layer, the trade-offs of each, and a recommendation, as [PROPUESTA].
STANDARD.questionnaire: Adaptive: asked for what the assessment found THIN or MISSING.

DEEP.for: complex, critical or highly uncertain systems
DEEP.assessment: Exhaustive: every area rated with its evidence, and architecture, non-functional requirements, security, data, integrations, deployment, observability, development architecture and constraints examined in depth.
DEEP.focus: alternatives, dependencies, risks, conflicts and gaps, each made explicit
DEEP.stack: Architectural alternatives as well as stack alternatives, the trade-offs of each explicit, every proposal traceable as [PROPUESTA].
DEEP.questionnaire: Deep and iterative: earlier answers are revisited when a later round changes them.

escalation.statement: When what the ADE finds justifies a deeper level, it proposes the escalation - one level at a time, with the evidence - and continues at the current level until the human decides. The ADE never raises or lowers the depth itself.
signals: availability, scale or performance requirements that constrain the architecture
documents that disagree on a structural point
a floor line not met with no obvious way to meet it
an architectural decision with high cost of reversal
escalation.recorded_as: a row of the escalation log in the assessment: from, to, evidence, and the human's decision (accepted or declined, who, date)

minimum_viable_design.becomes: source-material: reviewed by the human (Confirmation A), preserved verbatim as SOURCE-BRIEF.md; never governed architecture by being completed

lines: The problem and the scope are stated
The technology stack is decided: language and runtime, framework, where it runs
The datastore is decided, or the design states that it needs none
floor.same_as: the minimum floor of the Design Assessment
floor.readiness: READY and READY_WITH_OPEN_ITEMS require every line MET; a line is MET only when the human stated or confirmed it
